sentences.text:
This Petition, Coming On For Orders, This Day, The
Court Made The Following:
 Order

This writ petition is filed for following reliefs:
a) Issue a Writ of mandamus or any other writ of like nature and direct respondent no.2 to consider representation dated 08.02.2023 vide Annexure F given to respondent no.2 and consequently to pass award and pay compensation to petitioner or to return land in question to petitioners as prayed in same representation etc.

2. Sri Srinivas V., learned counsel for petitioners submitted that, Sri B.M. Javaregowda, father of petitioners purchased 10 guntas of land in Sy.no.96, situated at Koorgahalli village, Ilawala Hobli,
Mysore Taluk under registered sale deed dated 26.09.1991.
Thereafter, on 21.11.1995, he executed a Will bequeathing 5 guntas to each of petitioners and died on 04.08.2008.
3. It was submitted that respondents sought to acquire said land under Preliminary Notification dated 18.03.2006 and Final notification dated 05.12.2006.
It was NC: 2023:KHC:41165 submitted that their father had earlier submitted representation on 26.03.2008 (Annexure-D).
And on 08.02.2023, even petitioners gave representation (Annexure-F) to respondent no.2 for passing General award, as compensation offered under consent award was not satisfactory.
They also sought for allotment of alternative land in lieu of compensation.

It was submitted that under similar Thara @ Thara Subramanya vs Karnataka Industrial Areas ... on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101252781/
2 circumstances, this Court had allowed W.P.no.19563/2017 on 23.07.2019, directing respondent no.2 to pass General award and thereafter refer it for adjudication under Sections 30 and 31 of Land Acquisition Act.

sentences.text: Hence, sought for passing similar order.

4. On other hand, Sri P.V.Chandrashekar, learned counsel for respondents submitted that if reasonable time is granted, respondent no.2 would consider petitioners' representation, in accordance with law and sought for disposal of writ petition.

5. Heard learned counsel and perused writ petition record.
6.
From above submission, it is seen that land belonging to petitioners is sought to be acquired by respondents.

While, petitioners were not having any grievance NC: 2023:KHC:41165 against acquisition, they had only requested for passing General award and thereafter refer same for determination of market value by jurisdictional Reference Court.

7. Perusal of order passed in W.P.no.19563/2017 disposed of on 23.07.2019, would reveal that in similar circumstances, this Court had directed SLAO to pass General award and thereafter refer it for adjudication under Sections 30 and 31 of Land Acquisition Act.
Direction was also issued to conclude proceedings within four months after affording opportunity to all interested persons.

Since, facts of present case are similar to those in above writ petition, following same, I pass following:
ORDER Writ petition is disposed of directing respondent no.2 to consider petitioners' representation dated 08.02.2023 at Annexure-F, *for passing General Award within four months, after affording opportunity to all parties.* Sd/-
JUDGE
